back: A word that joins words, phrases or clauses and shows how the ideas relate.
notes: and, but, so, because, although, unless, when.

back: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so: they join clauses of equal importance.
notes: I was tired, but I finished.

back: because, although, if, unless, when, while, until, since, as soon as, so that: they begin a clause that cannot stand alone.
either ... or, neither ... nor, both ... and, not only ... but also, whether ... or.
notes: Neither Rudo nor her sister came.

back: however, therefore, moreover, nevertheless need a semicolon or full stop before them and usually a comma after them.
notes: The bus was late; however, we arrived on time.

back: Although ... (no but); Despite / In spite of + noun or -ing form.
notes: Although he trained, he lost. Despite training, he lost.

back: Addition: moreover, furthermore, in addition. Contrast: however, nevertheless, on the other hand. Result: therefore, consequently. Example: for instance. Conclusion: in conclusion, to sum up.
unless = if ... not. Never add not after it.
notes: Unless you hurry, you will miss the bus.

back: in case = as a precaution against something that may happen.
notes: Take an umbrella in case it rains.
